title: Dynamic tool adapter: streaming-compatible result passports and soft recursion fence
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: multi-tool chains that emit streaming deltas currently lack a robust, backward-compatible way to inject tool outputs into the conversational state while preventing runaway recursion. This ticket proposes a Dynamic Tool Adapter (DTA) layer that: 1) normalizes streaming frames from heterogeneous tool implementations into a small set of canonical frame types (partial, final, metadata, error), 2) attaches an opaque result passport that carries provenance, schema hints, and an idempotency token for safe replays/injections, 3) enforces a soft recursion fence using a combination of per-request recursion depth counters and adaptive backoff policy, and 4) exposes a compatibility shim for older tool specs that only support sync final outputs.

Design summary: the DTA sits between the orchestration runtime and tool runners. For streaming tools it multiplexes partial frames into the main response stream while tracking consistent schema annotations. The opaque passport is carried in the transport layer (HTTP headers / internal GRPC metadata) and persisted in the request session until canonicalized. Injection rules are deterministic: tool-provided final frames are eligible for injection only if the passport idempotency token is not already seen for the session and the recursion depth is below configured thresholds. For compatibility, the shim wraps legacy sync tool outputs into a single final frame with a generated passport and an annotation marking source compatibility mode.
acceptance_criteria: DTA implemented in runtime with streaming frame normalization and passport propagation
Idempotency passport prevents duplicate injections across retries and replays (unit + integration tests)
Recursion fence metrics: recursion depth and fence-trigger events emitted to telemetry and used to block escalation beyond threshold
Compatibility shim transparently converts legacy tool responses and passes existing tests for sync-only tools
Canary rollout plan and rollback implemented; feature flag guarded
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha: Initial RFC posted in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Dynamic+Tool+Adapter+RFC. Seeking feedback from runtime and SDK owners.

2026-03-03 - Martin: Spike complete; prototype normalizer in runtime branch 'dta-spike' https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128. Partial frames look good; need clearer schema hint format.
2026-03-05 - Lina Gomez (Design): Reviewed streaming UX for console logs. Recommend adding passport->human readable provenance mapping for debug view (console-2026.03#dta).
2026-03-07 - Security review kickoff: requested threat model for passport transport; we will encrypt passports at rest and scope them per-session. Security note added to RFC.

2026-03-09 - Martin: Implemented recursion fence counters and adaptive backoff. Observed repeated tool-invocation loops in synthetic load test; fence prevented escalation at depth 6. Telemetry event 'dta.recursion.fence_triggered' emitted.
2026-03-10 - PR opened for DTA core: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4281 — running CI. Requesting reviewers: @sophie-lee, @omar-rahman.
notes: Trade-offs: passports add metadata overhead (headers + storage) but keep runtime statelessness for most flows. Alternative was an in-memory-only recursion table — rejected because it broke cross-worker retry semantics.
Compatibility: shim will add ~2ms median latency for sync-to-stream conversion; acceptable for most internal tooling but flagged for high-qps endpoints.
Telemetry: add histograms for passport size, recursion depth, injection-latency, and number of suppressed injections per-session.
Rollout: feature-flagged behind 'dta.enabled'. Canary on dedicated pools for 72h with realtime dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/canaries/dta-canary
